research_questions.primary: To what extent can patient characteristics available near hospital admission predict length of stay in a real, de-identified hospital dataset, and how reliably can modern machine-learning models quantify uncertainty in those predictions?
research_questions.secondary: Do advanced nonlinear machine-learning models provide statistically meaningful predictive improvement over simple statistical and naive baselines?

data.dataset: UCI Diabetes 130-US Hospitals for Years 1999-2008 (real, de-identified; CC BY 4.0)

excluded.Race: not used as a predictor; used only to audit error parity
excluded.diag_2 / diag_3: secondary diagnoses are coded at discharge
excluded.set-B variables: accumulated during the stay or recorded at discharge

gamma_glm.diagnosis: converged with small train/validation gap; extra data unlikely to help (little learnable signal)

xgboost.diagnosis: converged with small train/validation gap; extra data unlikely to help (little learnable signal)

catboost.diagnosis: converged with small train/validation gap; extra data unlikely to help (little learnable signal)

ft_transformer.diagnosis: converged with small train/validation gap; extra data unlikely to help (little learnable signal)

selection.reason: 2.103-day nested-CV MAE makes 'xgboost' the point-estimate leader, but 4 of 7 models are statistically indistinguishable from it (corrected resampled t-test, p > 0.05, or within 0.022 days = 1% of baseline MAE). By parsimony the simplest of these, 'xgboost', is selected.

xgboost_aft.c_index_note: 0.5 = random ordering of stays; 1.0 = perfect ordering.

gamma_glm.c_index_note: 0.5 = random ordering of stays; 1.0 = perfect ordering.

null_comparison.interpretation: AIC/BIC lower for the null model means the added predictors do not improve the penalised likelihood enough to justify their parameters.

statistical_model.note: AIC, AICc and BIC compare likelihood-based models fitted to the same response and data. They are not reported for boosted trees or neural networks, whose effective number of parameters and likelihood are not comparable.

checks.label: Advanced models fail to meaningfully beat the median baseline
checks.pass_label: An advanced model beats the median baseline by at least 5% MAE (0.111 days)

checks.label: Bootstrap intervals show no meaningful difference between models
checks.pass_label: At least one advanced model is significantly better than the baseline (bootstrap CI below 0)

checks.label: Shuffled-target models perform similarly to real-target models
checks.pass_label: Real-target models clearly beat shuffled-target models (permutation p < 0.05)

checks.label: Prediction intervals are excessively wide
checks.pass_label: Prediction intervals are at least 10% narrower than a no-information interval

checks.label: Calibration is poor or predictions are non-discriminative
checks.pass_label: Predictions are calibrated (slope within 0.8-1.2) and discriminative
